name: Builder account
caveat: no account to run routed work as
detail: Creates the standard (not admin) account routed work runs as; sysadminctl asks for its password. An existing account is left alone.

name: Remote Login (ssh)
detail: Turns on Remote Login and admits the builder account to ssh (the com.apple.access_ssh group). Without it the PC cannot reach the Mac at all.

name: The PC's ssh key
detail: Appends the PC's public key (--public-key-file) to the builder's ~/.ssh/authorized_keys, folder 700 and file 600. Skip it only when the key is installed another way.

name: Tailscale (optional)
caveat: reach the builder on the LAN only
detail: Installs Homebrew's open-source tailscale, starts tailscaled with brew services and runs tailscale up; you sign in through the link it prints, and no auth key is ever taken. Skip it when the PC reaches the Mac on the LAN.

name: SSH for the builder user only
caveat: any account may log in over ssh
detail: Writes /etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/100-gate-prep.conf with AllowUsers for the builder and the admin running prep, checked with sshd -t. Every other account loses ssh; an AllowUsers rule from another file stops the step, to be merged by hand.

name: Xcode license accepted
caveat: builds that use Xcode tools fail
detail: Accepts the Xcode license, so builds that call Xcode's tools run. It skips itself when Xcode is not installed.

name: FileVault off
caveat: after a reboot the Mac waits at the unlock screen
detail: Turns FileVault off (fdesetup disable asks for an unlock credential), which lowers the security of the disk: whoever holds the Mac can read it. Automatic login needs FileVault off; leave it on when the Mac may leave your hands.

name: Automatic login
caveat: after a reboot routed runs wait for a person to log in
detail: Sets the login window's autoLoginUser, so the builder logs in by itself after a reboot or a power cut; the password, typed twice and checked, is stored only in /etc/kcpassword (root-only, reversibly encoded, as macOS automatic login requires). It needs FileVault off; re-run it with --force after a password change.
